phase_name: Gate 8's Serialized Isolation -- Decide on Evidence

objectives.description: Consult Phase 4's verdict; determine whether the drop-without-investigating condition applies
State why gate 8 is serialized today from the code; confirm which constraint it defends
Size the overlap opportunity (gate 8 alone vs. rest-of-pool wall clock) and evaluate oversubscription risk
Audit cache-store contention under an overlapped gate 8
Decide and record the outcome; close as COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS if the collision/risk is unresolved

approaches_tried.approach: Live measured overlap experiment (actually running gate 8 and the pool concurrently with a reduced shared worker budget)
approaches_tried.reason: Decided against on evidence before attempting: the sizing analysis (gate8 alone 663s vs. rest-of-pool 107s) bounds the maximum possible upside at ~14% of the total, and this host's live memory margin (5.3GB available, 7.4GB swapped) made deliberately adding more concurrent memory pressure an unjustified risk for that bounded a return, especially with no existing mechanism to coordinate a shared concurrency budget across two independent schedulers.

deviations.description: Consult Phase 4's verdict first; if BOTH exclusion conditions hold, close via that path
deviations.reason: Phase 4's verdict does not touch the serialization decision (condition 1 holds), but gate 8 is NOT rarely-executing under invalidation (condition 2 fails, same corpus-breadth argument as gate 3's Phase 11 measurement) -- so this phase proceeded past the first exclusion gate and closed instead via the separate 'collision/risk cannot be resolved' exclusion path at Task 12.5.
